records.title: Why You Can't Divide by Zero

assessedClaimEvidence.prompt: Match division by zero to its inverse multiplication question.: Which inverse equation would need a solution for 7 ÷ 0 to have a quotient?
Use the zero-product pattern.: What does 0 × any number equal?
Zero divided.: Five equal groups contain 0 counters in all. How many counters are in each group?
Zero as divisor again.: Does 12 ÷ 0 have a quotient?
Tell them apart.: Which expression has a quotient?

records.candidateEngineOrExtension: No manipulable engine change or additional transfer item is warranted. All assessed/exploratory items (i1, i2 mcq + k1, k2, k3 check + ch1 challenge) are deliberately conventional select/entry surfaces (mcq, numeric) because the concept — division by zero is undefined — is a symbolic, definitional exclusion proven by inverse multiplication (0 x ? = n has no solution), not a spatial or quantitative relationship a drag/build engine would model more truthfully. k1 (7÷0) and k3 (12÷0) share the DivZeroMcq generator form to drill the same undefined-quotient judgment at different numbers (near-repetition is intentional practice, not a flaw); k2 (0÷5=0, zero as dividend) and ch1 (discriminate 8÷0 vs 0÷8) are authored one-off conceptual items. This shape is test-locked by src/lib/session186.fluencyPair.test.ts (NO_FACT_LESSONS = {df3-03-02}; UNVARIANTED_OK includes df3-03-02/k2 and df3-03-02/ch1, documented there as 'one-off conceptual items') and src/lib/session254.divisionFluencyG3CourseIntegrity.test.tsx (option-id/length parity checks specifically pin df3-03-02/k1 and df3-03-02/k3).

authoredWrongPaths.feedback: This fact is true, but it does not find a number that zero can multiply to make 7.
This asks about 0 ÷ 7, where zero is the total, not the divisor.
If 7 ÷ 0 were 7, then 7 × 0 would have to equal 7, but 7 × 0 = 0.
If 7 ÷ 0 were 1, then 1 × 0 would have to equal 7, but 1 × 0 = 0.
If 7 ÷ 0 were 0, then 0 × 0 would have to equal 7, but 0 × 0 = 0.
Zero times any number is 0, so it cannot equal 12.
That repeats the divisor. Sharing nothing among 5 groups leaves nothing in each.
Zero shared into 5 groups gives 0 in each group, not 1.
If 12 ÷ 0 were 1, then 1 × 0 would have to equal 12, but 1 × 0 = 0.
If 12 ÷ 0 were 0, then 0 × 0 would have to equal 12, but 0 × 0 = 0.
If 12 ÷ 0 were 12, then 12 × 0 would have to equal 12, but 12 × 0 = 0.
Zero as the DIVISOR is undefined — no number times 0 gives 8.
Only division BY zero is undefined; zero divided by a number is simply 0.
